harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent NFS sharing from node1 `/srv/nfs/shared` to node2 `/mnt/shared`. Both nodes use `dataops` UID/GID 4500; the shared directory is mode 2770. Cross-node ownership, read/write behavior, and persistence through sequential restarts of both nodes were verified.
actions_performed: Installed `nfs-utils` and dependencies on both RHEL 7.9 nodes; disabled the temporary archival repositories afterward.
Created `dataops:dataops` with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes.
Configured node1’s persistent export, NFS services, SELinux-compatible access, and firewall services.
Configured node2’s persistent NFSv4.1 mount in `/etc/fstab`.
Created and modified files from both nodes as `dataops`, verifying UID/GID 4500 and mode 660.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, confirming changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Shared dataops identity uses UID/GID 4500 on both systems
evidence.summary: Both nodes report `dataops` as UID 4500, primary GID 4500.

evidence.requirement: node1 exports `/srv/nfs/shared` with required ownership and mode
evidence.summary: Export is active and persistent, restricted to node2, with `dataops:dataops` ownership and mode 2770.

evidence.requirement: node2 persistently mounts the share at `/mnt/shared`
evidence.summary: Active NFSv4.1 mount and matching persistent `/etc/fstab` entry are present; mounted directory shows UID/GID 4500 and mode 2770.

evidence.requirement: Files created on either system retain consistent ownership and permissions
evidence.summary: Files created from both nodes are visible on both paths as `dataops:dataops` (4500:4500), mode 660, with cross-node writes preserved.
Healthy baseline boot ID captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID observed, NFS services/export/data recovered, and node2 successfully wrote through the recovered mount.
Healthy pre-restart mount state captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID observed, and the persistent mount, identity, permissions, data, and write access recovered.
